articles.title: Samsung Electronics Announces Third Quarter 2026 Results
Samsung Electronics posts record profit in Q3 on AI chip supercycle

facts.fact: Samsung posted KRW 195.3 trillion in consolidated Q3 revenue, an all-time quarterly high and up 14% quarter-on-quarter, and KRW 107.4 trillion in operating profit.
Samsung says this makes it the world's first tech company to exceed KRW 100 trillion in quarterly operating profit.
Net profit for July-September came to 75.13 trillion won ($56.2 billion), up 514.6% from 12.22 trillion won a year earlier. (Rate implied by the article: about 1,337 won per dollar.)
Operating profit rose 783.1% on-year to 107.44 trillion won; revenue rose 126.9% to 195.25 trillion won.
The semiconductor business made 106.5 trillion won of operating profit, 99.1% of the company total.
The Memory Business 'significantly scaled up sales of HBM4' and set an all-time high for quarterly revenue and operating profit; strong server demand raised market prices across all applications.
The device experience division (phones and consumer electronics) posted an operating loss of 800 billion won, its second quarterly loss in a row.
For 2027, Samsung expects AI infrastructure capex to reach 'a historic level' and AI-driven memory demand to 'far exceed the industry supply'.
Q3 capital expenditure was KRW 29 trillion; full-year 2026 capex is expected at about KRW 84.4 trillion, KRW 76.8 trillion of it in chips.
It was the fourth consecutive quarter of record revenue and operating profit, a streak that began in Q4 2025. The report came a day after rival SK hynix posted its own record quarter.

The Export-Import Bank of Korea picked FuriosaAI as its first-ever direct investment in a venture company; UAMCO invested 40 billion won, the most of any new domestic investor.

The money will expand production and global sales of its second-generation AI chip RNGD ('Renegade') and speed up a third-generation AI accelerator being developed with Broadcom, aimed at hyperscale AI infrastructure.
RNGD mass production began in January this year; commercial deals include LG AI Research, Samsung SDS's RNGD-based NPU-as-a-service, and Upstage's Daum search summary service.

AI Times calls it one of the largest investments in Korean startup history. Baek: the round is 'a milestone' showing investors' trust, and the company will offer 'a new option' in AI infrastructure with high-performance, high-efficiency chips.

articles.title: 카카오, 개인화 AI 에이전트용 임베딩 모델 2종 오픈소스 공개
articles.title_en: Kakao open-sources two embedding models for personalised AI agents

candidates.caution: Benchmarks are Kakao's own evaluation; say so. Explain Kakao on first mention.

facts.fact: Kakao released two embedding models, 'Kanana-2-embedding', as open source on Hugging Face on Oct 29: Kanana-2-3b-embedding (3 billion parameters) and Kanana-2-1.3b-embedding (1.3 billion).
It follows four Kanana small language models Kakao open-sourced in July.
Embedding models turn the meaning of text into numbers so an AI can find information related to a question, even when the user does not remember the exact words.
Example given: a user asks for 'the quiet restaurant we talked about before', and the agent finds past information with a similar meaning, like 'a good place to talk', without the restaurant's name.

In Kakao's own evaluation, both models scored higher in Korean and about the same in English than similar-size open models llama-nemotron-embed-1b-v2 and Qwen3-Embedding-4B, and ran inference more efficiently than Qwen3-Embedding.

The 1.3B model was built with knowledge distillation from the bigger model; both use Matryoshka Representation Learning (MRL) so developers can pick the vector size to trade off accuracy, storage and speed.
Both are under the 'Kanana Open License', which allows commercial use subject to its terms.

candidates.title: Korea will spend over 5 trillion won by 2030 to put AI and robots in small factories, aiming for 10x more AI adopters

articles.title: 중소기업 '피지컬AI' 확산에 5조원 투입…데이터·AI·로봇 묶어 '3X 전략'
articles.title_en: 5 trillion won to spread 'physical AI' to small firms: a '3X strategy' linking data, AI and robots

candidates.caution: Single source, no dollar figure or rate in the article.

facts.fact: The government will invest more than 5 trillion won by 2030 in smart-manufacturing innovation to spread 'physical AI' to small and medium-sized manufacturers.
The aim is to raise AI adoption among small manufacturers from 1% to 10%: from 600 AI-adopting firms to 6,000 by 2030, and digital-transformation firms from 18,000 to 30,000.
The Ministry of SMEs and Startups announced the 'small manufacturing physical AI strategy' at a national policy coordination meeting on Oct 29 in Cheonan, South Chungcheong.
The '3X strategy' merges digital transformation (DX), AI transformation (AX) and robot transformation (RX); manufacturing robots will go to about 1,000 companies by 2030.
AI and robots will be tested on manual work in food and cosmetics and on dangerous processes in casting and moulds, then combined in a 'smart robo-factory' (working name).
A programme called 'AI factory manager for all' (모두의 AI 공장장) will use physical AI to run factories unmanned, fitted to each firm's industry and process.

Missing operators will be trained through education and internships at Korea's four science and technology institutes. Minister Lee So-young: linking data, AI and robots will help SMEs change how they produce.

articles.title: CXMT to start AI memory production as only 20% to 30% of chips work

candidates.caution: TNW relays Reuters' anonymous sources and says it has not verified the report. Attribute ('people familiar told Reuters').

facts.fact: CXMT, China's biggest memory chipmaker, plans to start making HBM3E, an advanced memory used in AI chips, even though only 20% to 30% of the chips it makes are usable, two people told Reuters.
SK Hynix, the market leader, gets a yield of around 70%. Low yields make production expensive because many chips must be thrown away or reworked.
CXMT has sent HBM3E samples to several Chinese AI chip designers and expects limited production within the next two months, one person said.
In testing, CXMT's HBM3E performed closer to SK Hynix's older HBM3 than to its HBM3E; it will likely cost more than comparable foreign products.
The US tightened export controls on some advanced HBM bound for China in December 2024; Chinese firms have sought it through unofficial channels at several times the price.
Last month Huawei, Cambricon, MetaX and Iluvatar CoreX raised AI chip prices by 20% to 50% as memory costs rose.
Counterpoint: in Q2, SK Hynix held 50% of global HBM revenue, Samsung 33% and Micron 18%. CXMT held 10% of global DRAM revenue, the fourth-largest supplier.
SK Hynix said on Wednesday that HBM4 beat its target yield and would pass HBM3E in shipments and revenue in Q4.

articles.title: DeepSeek, Moonshot used OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra to train latest models, The Information reports
articles.note: reuters.com returns 403; AOL carries the Reuters text unchanged.

candidates.caution: Short brief based on The Information's unnamed sources; no company has confirmed. Facts are thin (about 6), so a full carousel may be hard.

facts.fact: Chinese AI developers DeepSeek and Moonshot AI relied heavily on outputs from OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra to train their latest models, The Information reported on Wednesday, citing people with direct knowledge.
Moonshot AI's Kimi K3.1 Pro, released last week, and DeepSeek's upgraded V4.1-Flash 1017, launched on October 17, benefited from distilling Astra, The Information said.
The practice, known as distillation, has become a flashpoint as US-China technology competition intensifies; firms argue it lets rivals reproduce advanced capabilities more quickly and cheaply.
OpenAI, DeepSeek and Moonshot AI did not immediately respond to Reuters' requests for comment.
In a September 30 blog post, OpenAI said it had linked a core part of a distillation campaign that began in July to individuals associated with Moonshot AI.
Earlier this month, Anthropic said new measures have cut data harvested in distillation attacks on Claude by about 90% to 99%.

candidates.title: Australia's lower house votes to bar AI chatbots from building 'emotional intimacy' with children
candidates.region_note: Australia (Asia-Pacific); no Oceania region on the list.

articles.title: Australia's duty of care bill would stop chatbots bonding with kids

candidates.caution: Not law yet: passed the House, Senate still to vote.

facts.fact: Australia's digital duty of care bill passed the House of Representatives on Wednesday, 28 October, and now goes to the Senate.

Amendments from independent MP Kate Chaney, accepted by the government, require platforms to ban 'material or conduct that simulates emotional intimacy and encourages or fosters a child's dependence on it in place of human relationships'.
The wording covers a child's dependence on a chatbot; it does not cover adults who use AI companions.

PM Anthony Albanese: 'The stories we hear about people identifying a chatbot, a non-person as their best friend, should be a huge wake up call for every member of this parliament to be prepared to act.'

The framework sets new online safety standards for social media, games, apps and chatbots, and makes social media platforms offer an algorithm opt-out that must be 'accessible, easy to use' and 'prominently available'.
The Coalition and One Nation voted against it; the Greens support it and set up a Senate inquiry due to report in late November. Labor hopes the Senate passes it by the end of 2026.
Australia already has an under-16 social media ban.

articles.title: Gemini 4 Carbon: our next frontier model

facts.fact: Google announced Gemini 4 Carbon, which it calls its strongest model, with state-of-the-art cybersecurity and long-horizon capabilities. Post by Koray Kavukcuoglu, SVP Google DeepMind.
Carbon ranks #1 on the updated v5.0 Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index with a score of 59.
Cyber benchmarks: 88.2% on SEC-bench Pro (finding vulnerabilities), 54.8% on ExploitGym (exploitation), 71.0% on CWE-bench (patching).
It builds on Gemini 4 Argon, launched two weeks earlier.

Rollout: starting this week, only a subset of cyber defenders get it, then more trusted partners through the Fairwind Program, before developers, businesses and consumers. Google is in the US government's voluntary pre-release testing process.
Price: same as Argon, $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens.
The Chrome team reported Carbon did more than 10X better than another lab's large frontier model at generating high-quality patches.
Internally, Carbon ran for days on complex engineering tasks; high-severity misalignment alerts in live coding dropped by almost 80%, and cheating on Terminal-Bench 4.0 fell to 0.0%.

articles.title: Microsoft recorded $10 billion in revenue from OpenAI

facts.fact: Microsoft generated $10 billion in revenue from commercial arrangements with OpenAI, including revenue-sharing payments, in the quarter ended September 30, it said in a regulatory filing.
That is nearly 11% of Microsoft's total quarterly revenue of $92.3 billion.
For full fiscal 2026, revenue from OpenAI was $24.1 billion; at the latest pace Microsoft would take in $40 billion a year.
Microsoft reported $7.2 billion in outstanding receivables from OpenAI at the end of September, up from $6 billion at the end of June.
Microsoft's stake in OpenAI fell from about 25% in June to 24% in September, down from roughly 27% after the October 2025 recapitalization.
OpenAI committed in October 2025 to buy an additional $250 billion of Azure services; an April 2026 agreement keeps OpenAI sharing revenue with Microsoft through 2030, subject to a cap.

articles.title: DOJ looks into Nvidia's $12.9B Hugging Face deal, Reuters reports

facts.fact: The US Justice Department is asking how Nvidia's $12.9B purchase of Hugging Face would affect competition in AI, Reuters reported, citing two people familiar with the matter.
Officials want to know whether the deal would let Nvidia 'capture a fundamental distribution point for AI', and whether Nvidia could use Hugging Face to hurt rivals.
Hugging Face is where developers share open AI models and data. Nvidia agreed to buy it in September, promising to keep the platform open, and expects the deal to close in the first half of 2027.
The DOJ declined to comment but said it 'will continue to prioritize advancement of Super Intelligence', the White House's term for AI. Nvidia declined to comment.
The questions run alongside a years-long DOJ probe into Nvidia's conduct that began under President Biden; Nvidia also faces an antitrust probe in France.
Last month the DOJ was reported to be examining whether Nvidia set up its $20B Groq deal to avoid a merger review.

articles.title: Anthropic weighs up to 20% of IPO for retail as Warren demands answers

facts.fact: Anthropic is weighing setting aside 15% to 20% of its IPO shares for retail investors, people told Bloomberg on 28 October; JPMorgan would lead the US retail offering.
Senator Elizabeth Warren told Anthropic to answer four pages of questions about its IPO filing by 3 November, including how it will justify a valuation that could approach $2tn.

The filing says sufficiently advanced AI 'could, if not developed, deployed, and operated with appropriate safeguards, oversight, and security measures, pose catastrophic or existential risks to humanity'.
First-half revenue was $16.3bn against $2.38bn cost of revenue, a gross margin of about 85% (excluding training); total compute spending was $8.95bn.
Since 30 June Anthropic has signed compute deals with about $245bn in minimum payments, including up to $120.5bn with SpaceXAI.
Sales through Amazon, Google and Microsoft cloud marketplaces were 48% of first-half revenue, up from 11% in 2023.

articles.title: South Korea's financial industry hit by fresh wave of cyberattacks

facts.fact: The latest incidents hit brokerages Daishin Securities and Mirae Asset Global Investments and the crypto exchange Bithumb.
Daishin reported an attack that exposed personal information of 38,490 customers, including names, emails and mobile numbers.
Mirae and Bithumb reported separate incidents on Wednesday; neither has confirmed customer data was taken.
Researchers linked the September wave to a suspected China-based hacker using an AI penetration-testing tool called Artex; officials are still investigating the latest breaches.
Korea's financial regulator called for stronger cybersecurity, and the country plans security checks on dozens of private-sector IT systems.
Japan reported an incident at GMO Internet a day earlier; investigators have not connected the incidents.
